    # Part II — The program
    
    Single translation unit, FLINT for all number theory (`n_primes_t`, `n_factor`, `n_powmod2`, `n_lcm`, `n_remove`, `fmpz_root`, `fmpz_remove`, `fmpz_powm_ui`, `fmpz_val2`, `fmpz_is_prime`), `std::thread` for parallelism. No composite‑`q` reporting, no ruled‑out cases, one funnel.
    
    ```cpp
    /* =====================================================================
       twinrep.cpp —  p = 2^m1 + q^n1 = 2^m2 + q^n2, same prime base q,
                      open case:  A > 1,  Δm even,  Δn odd.
       Exhausts all p < 10^D (default D = 256, i.e. m1 ≤ 850).
    
       Build:
         g++ -O3 -march=native -std=c++17 -pthread twinrep.cpp -lflint -lmpfr -lgmp -o twinrep
       Run:
         ./twinrep --digits 256 --Q 100000000 --threads 24 --verbose
    
       Structure (see synthesis):
         * a pair (q, Δm) with q | 2^Δm − 1 determines m2 = v2(q−1),
           n1 = v_q(2^Δm−1), A = (2^Δm−1)/q^{n1}; a configuration exists iff
           A·2^{m2}+1 is an odd power of q.  core_test() decides one pair.
         * regime A enumerates q ≤ Q from a precomputed ord_ℓ(2) table;
         * regime B enumerates q > Q as forced n2-th roots of 2^m1 − 2^m2.
       ===================================================================== */
    
    #include <flint/flint.h>
    #include <flint/fmpz.h>
    #include <flint/ulong_extras.h>
    
    #include <cstdio>
    #include <cstdlib>
    #include <cstring>
    #include <cmath>
    #include <string>
    #include <vector>
    #include <thread>
    #include <mutex>
    #include <atomic>
    #include <algorithm>
    #include <chrono>
    
    /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ cfg */
    struct Cfg {
        int      digits  = 256;
        slong    Mmax    = 0;          /* ceiling on m1 = floor(log2 p) */
        ulong    Q       = 100000000UL;/* small/large split for q        */
        int      threads = 0;
        int      verbose = 0;
    };
    static Cfg cfg;
    
    /* ------------------------------------------------------- funnel stages */
    enum {
        ST_PAIR = 0, ST_SIZE, ST_RANGE, ST_MOD3, ST_ORD2, ST_PRIME, ST_UDIV,
        ST_N1PAR, ST_ODDORD, ST_WINDOW, ST_VAL, ST_EXACT, ST_HIT, ST_N
    };
    static const char *STNAME[ST_N] = {
        "pairs (q,dm) examined",
        "S1  q^3 < 2^dm                      (§9.3,§9.4)",
        "S2  m2 = v2(q-1) <= k, m1 <= Mmax    (§5.2,§9.2 E3)",
        "S3  q = 3 or q = 1 mod 3             (§1 = §5.4 at l=3)",
        "S4  q | 2^dm - 1                     (§5.3)",
        "S5  q prime",
        "S6  u | 2^dm - 1, u = odd part q-1   (§8.1,§8.2)",
        "S7  parity of n1 vs q mod 8          (§7.1,§7.2)",
        "S8  ord_l(q) odd for all l in S      (§5.4,§10.2)",
        "S9  odd dn, L | dn, inside window    (§9.5,§10.3)",
        "S10 valuation identity on dn         (§8.3)",
        "S11 exact  A*2^m2 + 1 = q^dn         (§5.3)",
        "S12 p prime and both representations verified"
    };
    
    /* ------------------------------------------------ ord_l(2) prime table */
    struct PrimeRec {
        ulong l;
        ulong e;                 /* ord_l(2)                 */
        std::vector<ulong> rf;   /* distinct primes of l - 1 */
    };
    static std::vector<PrimeRec> TAB;
    
    static inline ulong ord_mod_prime(ulong l, ulong b, const std::vector<ulong> &rf)
    {                                   /* order of b (!=0) modulo prime l */
        ulong d = l - 1;
        for (ulong r : rf)
            while (d % r == 0 && n_powmod2(b, (slong)(d / r), l) == 1) d /= r;
        return d;
    }
    
    static void factor_distinct(ulong n, std::vector<ulong> &out)
    {
        out.clear();
        n_factor_t f; n_factor_init(&f); n_factor(&f, n, 1);
        for (int i = 0; i < f.num; i++) out.push_back(f.p[i]);
    }
    
    static const PrimeRec *tab_lookup(ulong l)
    {
        auto it = std::lower_bound(TAB.begin(), TAB.end(), l,
                  [](const PrimeRec &a, ulong v){ return a.l < v; });
        if (it != TAB.end() && it->l == l) return &*it;
        return nullptr;
    }
    
    /* ord_l(2) for an arbitrary small prime l (table first, else compute) */
    static ulong ord2_of(ulong l)
    {
        const PrimeRec *pr = tab_lookup(l);
        if (pr) return pr->e;
        std::vector<ulong> rf; factor_distinct(l - 1, rf);
        return ord_mod_prime(l, 2 % l, rf);
    }
    
    static void build_table(int nthreads)
    {
        auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        const ulong Q = cfg.Q;
        std::vector<std::vector<PrimeRec>> part(nthreads);
        std::vector<std::thread> th;
        ulong span = Q / nthreads + 1;
    
        for (int t = 0; t < nthreads; t++) {
            th.emplace_back([&, t]() {
                ulong lo = 3 + (ulong)t * span, hi = std::min<ulong>(Q, lo + span - 1);
                if (lo > Q) { flint_cleanup(); return; }
                n_primes_t it; n_primes_init(it);
                n_primes_jump_after(it, lo - 1);
                std::vector<ulong> rf;
                for (ulong l = n_primes_next(it); l <= hi; l = n_primes_next(it)) {
                    if (l == 2) continue;
                    factor_distinct(l - 1, rf);
                    ulong e = ord_mod_prime(l, 2, rf);
                    if ((slong)e <= cfg.Mmax) part[t].push_back({l, e, rf});
                }
                n_primes_clear(it);
                flint_cleanup();
            });
        }
        for (auto &x : th) x.join();
        for (auto &v : part) TAB.insert(TAB.end(), v.begin(), v.end());
        std::sort(TAB.begin(), TAB.end(),
                  [](const PrimeRec &a, const PrimeRec &b){ return a.l < b.l; });
        double s = std::chrono::duration<double>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - t0).count();
        std::printf("table: %zu primes l <= %llu with ord_l(2) <= %ld   (%.1f s)\n",
                    TAB.size(), (unsigned long long)cfg.Q, (long)cfg.Mmax, s);
        std::fflush(stdout);
    }
    
    /* -------------------------------------------------------------- output */
    struct LiveRec {                 /* every pair that survives S8 */
        slong dm, m2, n1; std::string q;
        int    nS; ulong L; int ndn; std::string dns; int stage;
    };
    struct Hit { std::string p, q, A; slong m1, m2, n1, n2; int pprime; };
    
    static std::mutex g_mu;
    static std::vector<LiveRec> g_live;
    static std::vector<Hit>     g_hits;
    
    static std::string fstr(const fmpz_t x)
    { char *s = fmpz_get_str(NULL, 10, x); std::string r(s); flint_free(s); return r; }
    
    /* ------------------------------------------------------- scratch space */
    struct Work {
        fmpz_t M, t, t2, A, T, P, LB, UB, qm1, u, q, N, r;
        Work()  { fmpz_init(M); fmpz_init(t); fmpz_init(t2); fmpz_init(A);
                  fmpz_init(T); fmpz_init(P); fmpz_init(LB); fmpz_init(UB);
                  fmpz_init(qm1); fmpz_init(u); fmpz_init(q); fmpz_init(N); fmpz_init(r); }
        ~Work() { fmpz_clear(M); fmpz_clear(t); fmpz_clear(t2); fmpz_clear(A);
                  fmpz_clear(T); fmpz_clear(P); fmpz_clear(LB); fmpz_clear(UB);
                  fmpz_clear(qm1); fmpz_clear(u); fmpz_clear(q); fmpz_clear(N); fmpz_clear(r); }
    };
    
    /* =====================================================================
       core_test:  decide the pair (q, dm) completely.
       cand = all primes l <= Q dividing 2^dm - 1 (partial S is sound).
       Returns the stage at which the pair dies, or ST_HIT.
       ===================================================================== */
    static int core_test(Work &W, const fmpz_t q, slong dm,
                         const std::vector<const PrimeRec *> &cand,
                         uint64_t *passed)
    {
        const slong k = dm / 2;
        passed[ST_PAIR]++;
    
        LiveRec lr; bool track = false;
        auto ret = [&](int s) -> int {
            if (track) { lr.stage = s; std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_mu); g_live.push_back(lr); }
            return s;
        };
    
        /* M = 2^dm - 1 */
        fmpz_one(W.M); fmpz_mul_2exp(W.M, W.M, dm); fmpz_sub_ui(W.M, W.M, 1);
    
        /* ---- S1  q^3 < 2^dm  (Dn >= 3 together with q^Dn < 2^dm) */
        fmpz_pow_ui(W.t, q, 3);
        if (fmpz_cmp(W.t, W.M) > 0) return ret(ST_SIZE);
        passed[ST_SIZE]++;
    
        /* ---- S2  m2 = v2(q-1) <= k and m1 in range */
        fmpz_sub_ui(W.qm1, q, 1);
        slong m2 = fmpz_val2(W.qm1);
        slong m1 = m2 + dm;
        if (m2 > k || m1 > cfg.Mmax) return ret(ST_RANGE);
        passed[ST_RANGE]++;
    
        /* ---- S3  mod 3 */
        if (!(fmpz_fdiv_ui(q, 3) == 1 || fmpz_equal_ui(q, 3))) return ret(ST_MOD3);
        passed[ST_MOD3]++;
    
        /* ---- S4  q | 2^dm - 1 */
        fmpz_set_ui(W.t, 2); fmpz_powm_ui(W.t, W.t, dm, q);
        if (!fmpz_is_one(W.t)) return ret(ST_ORD2);
        passed[ST_ORD2]++;
    
        /* ---- S5  q prime */
        if (!fmpz_is_probabprime(q)) return ret(ST_PRIME);
        passed[ST_PRIME]++;
    
        /* ---- S6  u | 2^dm - 1,  u = odd part of q-1  (no factorisation) */
        fmpz_fdiv_q_2exp(W.u, W.qm1, m2);
        if (!fmpz_is_one(W.u)) {
            fmpz_set_ui(W.t, 2); fmpz_powm_ui(W.t, W.t, dm, W.u);
            if (!fmpz_is_one(W.t)) return ret(ST_UDIV);
        }
        passed[ST_UDIV]++;
    
        /* ---- S7  n1 and its parity against q mod 8 */
        slong n1 = fmpz_remove(W.A, W.M, q);     /* A = (2^dm-1)/q^{n1} */
        ulong q8 = fmpz_fdiv_ui(q, 8);
        if (q8 == 3 && (n1 & 1) == 0) return ret(ST_N1PAR);
        if (q8 == 7 && (n1 & 1) == 1) return ret(ST_N1PAR);
        passed[ST_N1PAR]++;
    
        /* ---- S8  odd-order closure, and L = lcm of the orders */
        ulong L = 1; int nS = 0; bool Lbig = false;
        for (const PrimeRec *pr : cand) {
            ulong l = pr->l;
            if (fmpz_equal_ui(q, l)) continue;                 /* l = q    */
            ulong b = fmpz_fdiv_ui(q, l);
            if (b == 1) continue;                              /* l | q-1  */
            ulong o = ord_mod_prime(l, b, pr->rf);
            if ((o & 1) == 0) return ret(ST_ODDORD);           /* §5.4 kill */
            nS++;
            if (!Lbig) { L = n_lcm(L, o); if (L > (ulong)(2 * cfg.Mmax)) Lbig = true; }
        }
        passed[ST_ODDORD]++;
        track = true;
        lr.dm = dm; lr.m2 = m2; lr.n1 = n1; lr.q = fstr(q);
        lr.nS = nS; lr.L = Lbig ? 0 : L; lr.ndn = 0; lr.dns = "";
    
        /* ---- S9  window:  2^{m2}(2^k - 1) < q^dn < 2^{2k},  dn odd, L | dn */
        fmpz_one(W.t); fmpz_mul_2exp(W.t, W.t, k); fmpz_sub_ui(W.t, W.t, 1);
        fmpz_mul_2exp(W.LB, W.t, m2); fmpz_add_ui(W.LB, W.LB, 1);   /* q^dn >= LB */
        fmpz_one(W.UB); fmpz_mul_2exp(W.UB, W.UB, dm);              /* q^dn <  UB */
    
        std::vector<slong> dns;
        fmpz_one(W.P);
        for (slong dn = 1;; dn++) {
            fmpz_mul(W.P, W.P, q);
            if (fmpz_cmp(W.P, W.UB) >= 0) break;
            if (fmpz_cmp(W.P, W.LB) < 0)  continue;
            if ((dn & 1) && dn >= 3 && !Lbig && (dn % (slong)L == 0)) dns.push_back(dn);
        }
        if (dns.empty()) return ret(ST_WINDOW);
        passed[ST_WINDOW]++;
        { std::string s; for (slong d : dns) { s += std::to_string(d); s += ' '; }
          lr.ndn = (int)dns.size(); lr.dns = s; }
    
        /* ---- S10  valuation identity (§8.3), when q-1 is factorable cheaply */
        if (fmpz_abs_fits_ui(W.qm1)) {
            std::vector<ulong> fac; factor_distinct(fmpz_get_ui(W.qm1), fac);
            for (ulong l : fac) {
                if (l == 2) continue;
                ulong e = ord2_of(l);
                fmpz_one(W.t); fmpz_mul_2exp(W.t, W.t, e); fmpz_sub_ui(W.t, W.t, 1);
                fmpz_set_ui(W.t2, l);
                slong v1 = fmpz_remove(W.t, W.t, W.t2);            /* v_l(2^e - 1) */
                ulong xx = (ulong)dm;  slong vdm = n_remove(&xx, l);
                slong vq = fmpz_remove(W.t, W.qm1, W.t2);          /* v_l(q-1)     */
                slong need = v1 + vdm - vq;
                std::vector<slong> keep;
                for (slong dn : dns) {
                    ulong y = (ulong)dn; slong v = n_remove(&y, l);
                    if (need >= 0 && v == need) keep.push_back(dn);
                }
                dns.swap(keep);
                if (dns.empty()) break;
            }
            if (dns.empty()) return ret(ST_VAL);
        }
        passed[ST_VAL]++;
    
        /* ---- S11  exact test:  T = A*2^{m2} + 1 must be an odd power of q */
        fmpz_mul_2exp(W.T, W.A, m2); fmpz_add_ui(W.T, W.T, 1);
        slong dn = fmpz_remove(W.t, W.T, q);
        if (!fmpz_is_one(W.t) || dn < 3 || (dn & 1) == 0) return ret(ST_EXACT);
        passed[ST_EXACT]++;
    
        /* ---- S12  reconstruct and verify p */
        slong n2 = n1 + dn;
        fmpz_pow_ui(W.P, q, n2);
        fmpz_one(W.t); fmpz_mul_2exp(W.t, W.t, m2);
        fmpz_add(W.T, W.P, W.t);                                   /* p = 2^m2 + q^n2 */
        fmpz_pow_ui(W.t2, q, n1);
        fmpz_one(W.t); fmpz_mul_2exp(W.t, W.t, m1);
        fmpz_add(W.t, W.t, W.t2);                                  /* 2^m1 + q^n1     */
        int ok = fmpz_equal(W.t, W.T);
        int pp = ok ? fmpz_is_prime(W.T) : 0;
        if (ok && pp) passed[ST_HIT]++;
        {
            Hit h; h.p = fstr(W.T); h.q = fstr(q); h.A = fstr(W.A);
            h.m1 = m1; h.m2 = m2; h.n1 = n1; h.n2 = n2; h.pprime = pp;
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_mu); g_hits.push_back(h);
        }
        return ret(ST_HIT);
    }
    
    /* ------------------------------------ candidate small primes for one dm */
    static void candidates_for(slong dm, std::vector<const PrimeRec *> &out)
    {
        out.clear();
        for (const PrimeRec &pr : TAB)
            if (dm % (slong)pr.e == 0) out.push_back(&pr);
    }
    
    /* ======================= regime A:  q <= Q, from the table ============ */
    static void regimeA(int nthreads, std::vector<std::array<uint64_t, ST_N>> &st)
    {
        std::atomic<slong> next{6};
        std::vector<std::thread> th;
        for (int t = 0; t < nthreads; t++) {
            th.emplace_back([&, t]() {
                Work W; std::vector<const PrimeRec *> cand;
                for (;;) {
                    slong dm = next.fetch_add(2);
                    if (dm > cfg.Mmax - 1) break;
                    candidates_for(dm, cand);
                    fmpz_t q; fmpz_init(q);
                    for (const PrimeRec *pr : cand) {
                        fmpz_set_ui(q, pr->l);
                        core_test(W, q, dm, cand, st[t].data());
                    }
                    fmpz_clear(q);
                }
                flint_cleanup();
            });
        }
        for (auto &x : th) x.join();
    }
    
    /* ========= regime B:  q > Q, forced as ceil(N^{1/n2}), N = 2^m1 - 2^m2 = */
    static void regimeB(int nthreads, std::vector<std::array<uint64_t, ST_N>> &st,
                        std::vector<uint64_t> &triples)
    {
        const double lgQ = std::log2((double)cfg.Q);
        std::atomic<slong> next{6};
        std::vector<std::thread> th;
        for (int t = 0; t < nthreads; t++) {
            th.emplace_back([&, t]() {
                Work W; std::vector<const PrimeRec *> cand;
                fmpz_t Mn; fmpz_init(Mn);
                for (;;) {
                    slong dm = next.fetch_add(2);
                    if (dm > cfg.Mmax - 1) break;
                    slong k = dm / 2;
                    candidates_for(dm, cand);
                    fmpz_one(Mn); fmpz_mul_2exp(Mn, Mn, dm); fmpz_sub_ui(Mn, Mn, 1);
    
                    slong m2hi = std::min<slong>(k, cfg.Mmax - dm);
                    for (slong m2 = 1; m2 <= m2hi; m2++) {
                        slong m1 = m2 + dm;
                        fmpz_mul_2exp(W.N, Mn, m2);                 /* N = 2^m1 - 2^m2 */
                        slong n2lo = std::max<slong>(4, (slong)std::floor(3.0 * (m1 - 1) / dm));
                        slong n2hi = (slong)std::floor((m1 + 1) / lgQ) + 1;
                        for (slong n2 = n2lo; n2 <= n2hi; n2++) {
                            fmpz_root(W.r, W.N, n2);                /* floor root      */
                            fmpz_add_ui(W.q, W.r, 1);               /* q = ceil root   */
                            if (fmpz_cmp_ui(W.q, cfg.Q) <= 0) continue;  /* regime A    */
                            if (fmpz_is_even(W.q)) continue;
                            triples[t]++;
                            core_test(W, W.q, dm, cand, st[t].data());
                        }
                    }
                }
                fmpz_clear(Mn);
                flint_cleanup();
            });
        }
        for (auto &x : th) x.join();
    }
    
    /* ------------------------------------------------------------- reports */
    static void print_funnel(const char *name, const std::array<uint64_t, ST_N> &p)
    {
        std::printf("\n=== funnel, %s ===\n", name);
        for (int s = 0; s < ST_N; s++)
            std::printf("  %-52s %12llu\n", STNAME[s], (unsigned long long)p[s]);
    }
    
    int main(int argc, char **argv)
    {
        for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
            auto val = [&](void) -> const char * { return argv[++i]; };
            if      (!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--digits"))  cfg.digits  = std::atoi(val());
            else if (!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--mmax"))    cfg.Mmax    = std::atol(val());
            else if (!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--Q"))       cfg.Q       = std::strtoull(val(), 0, 10);
            else if (!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--threads")) cfg.threads = std::atoi(val());
            else if (!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--verbose")) cfg.verbose = 1;
            else { std::fprintf(stderr, "unknown option %s\n", argv[i]); return 1; }
        }
        if (!cfg.Mmax) cfg.Mmax = (slong)std::floor(cfg.digits * std::log2(10.0));
        int nthreads = cfg.threads ? cfg.threads : (int)std::thread::hardware_concurrency();
        if (nthreads <= 0) nthreads = 1;
    
        std::printf(
    "twinrep: open case  A > 1,  Dm even,  Dn odd  (Dm odd: mod 3; Dn even: §6.4;\n"
    "         A = 1: p = 11 by Mihailescu).  p < 10^%d  <=>  m1 = floor(log2 p) <= %ld.\n"
    "         split Q = %llu, threads = %d\n",
            cfg.digits, (long)cfg.Mmax, (unsigned long long)cfg.Q, nthreads);
    
        auto T0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        build_table(nthreads);
    
        std::vector<std::array<uint64_t, ST_N>> stA(nthreads), stB(nthreads);
        for (auto &a : stA) a.fill(0);
        for (auto &a : stB) a.fill(0);
        std::vector<uint64_t> triples(nthreads, 0);
    
        auto t1 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        regimeA(nthreads, stA);
        auto t2 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        regimeB(nthreads, stB, triples);
        auto t3 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    
        std::array<uint64_t, ST_N> A{}, B{}; A.fill(0); B.fill(0);
        for (auto &v : stA) for (int s = 0; s < ST_N; s++) A[s] += v[s];
        for (auto &v : stB) for (int s = 0; s < ST_N; s++) B[s] += v[s];
        uint64_t trip = 0; for (uint64_t x : triples) trip += x;
    
        print_funnel("regime A  (q <= Q, §5.3 decision procedure)", A);
        std::printf("  [%.1f s]\n", std::chrono::duration<double>(t2 - t1).count());
        print_funnel("regime B  (q > Q, q forced as ceil(N^{1/n2}))", B);
        std::printf("  triples (dm,m2,n2) scanned: %llu   [%.1f s]\n",
                    (unsigned long long)trip, std::chrono::duration<double>(t3 - t2).count());
    
        std::sort(g_live.begin(), g_live.end(),
                  [](const LiveRec &a, const LiveRec &b){
                      return a.dm != b.dm ? a.dm < b.dm : a.q < b.q; });
        std::printf("\n=== pairs surviving the odd-order closure S8 (§5.4): %zu ===\n", g_live.size());
        std::printf("%6s %24s %5s %5s %4s %8s %5s  %-12s %s\n",
                    "dm", "q", "m2", "n1", "|S|", "L", "#dn", "dn list", "died at");
        for (const LiveRec &r : g_live)
            std::printf("%6ld %24s %5ld %5ld %4d %8llu %5d  %-12s %s\n",
                        (long)r.dm, r.q.c_str(), (long)r.m2, (long)r.n1, r.nS,
                        (unsigned long long)r.L, r.ndn, r.dns.c_str(), STNAME[r.stage]);
    
        std::printf("\n=== configurations found: %zu ===\n", g_hits.size());
        for (const Hit &h : g_hits)
            std::printf("  p = %s  (%zu digits, prime=%d)  q = %s  m1=%ld m2=%ld n1=%ld n2=%ld  A = %s\n",
                        h.p.c_str(), h.p.size(), h.pprime, h.q.c_str(),
                        (long)h.m1, (long)h.m2, (long)h.n1, (long)h.n2, h.A.c_str());
        if (g_hits.empty())
            std::printf("  none: no prime p < 10^%d has two representations with a common\n"
                        "  base q and A > 1.  (A = 1 gives p = 11 unconditionally.)\n", cfg.digits);
    
        std::printf("\ntotal %.1f s\n", std::chrono::duration<double>(
                        std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - T0).count());
        flint_cleanup_master();
        return 0;
    }

    # Part III — Using it
    
    **Build**
    
    ```
    g++ -O3 -march=native -std=c++17 -pthread twinrep.cpp -lflint -lmpfr -lgmp -o twinrep
    ./twinrep --digits 256 --Q 100000000 --threads 24 --verbose
    ```
    
    On a 5900X the table build (primes ≤ 10⁸, `ord_ℓ(2) ≤ 850`) dominates at a few tens of seconds; regime A is instantaneous (≈ a few thousand pairs); regime B is a couple of million forced roots, a minute or two. **256 digits is a coffee break, not two days.** `--digits 1000` (`M = 3322`) costs roughly `M³/log₂Q` root extractions on ~3300‑bit numbers — a few hours; `--Q 1000000000` buys a sharper `S(q,Δm)` and a smaller regime B at the cost of ~2 min more table build.
    
    **What to read in the output**
    
    * The funnel is sequential, not marginal: each line is the number of pairs that survived *everything above it*. S1–S7 are local congruence/valuation pins; S8 is the closure condition internal to `2^Δm−1`; S9 is the Archimedean window. The interesting number is how many pairs reach S8 and S9 at all.
    * The **S8 survivor table** is the evidence for lemma **L2**: empirically these are precisely the `q = 2^k − 1`, `Δm = 2k` configurations (`|S| ≤ 1`, `L ∈ {1, small odd}`), and every one of them dies at S9 with an empty window — the closed‑form elimination of §5.5 reappearing as an instance of the general criterion. If that pattern holds out to `Δm = 849`, you have the empirical shape of the induction you need: *`S` small ⇒ `q^{n1}` nearly fills `2^k ± 1` ⇒ `log₂q ≥ k − m2` ⇒ window contains no integer.*
    * Any line reaching S10/S11 is a genuinely hard configuration and would be the object of a hand proof; a line reaching S12 would be a counterexample to the conjecture.
    
    **What the run certifies (theorem form).** For all `p < 10^D`: if `p` has two representations `2^{m1}+q^{n1} = 2^{m2}+q^{n2}` with a common prime base `q`, then `A = 1` and `p = 11`. The proof is: R1–R3 above reduce to the even/odd case with `A > 1`; §1 of this synthesis shows such a case is determined by `(q, Δm)` with `q | 2^Δm − 1`, `Δm` even, `Δm ≤ M−1`; regime A exhausts `q ≤ Q` (completeness of the `ord_ℓ(2)` table), regime B exhausts `q > Q` (the forced‑root lemma plus `n2 < (m1+1)/log₂Q`); `core_test` is an exact decision for each pair. The filters S1–S10 are only accelerators — the verdict always comes from S11.

    # Exponent-space covering experiment — plan
    
    ## Status / corrections (read first)
    - **Direction:** exponent-space covering systems — arithmetic progressions in the exponent `m`
      that force `p − 2ᵐ` to always factor. This is the de Polignac / Erdős covering-congruence
      structure. It has a real payoff (the covering system + the primes it certifies).
    - **The certificate (value-space, `x ≡ 0 mod q` for all primes `q ≤ √p_max`) is REJECTED** —
      verified numbers are in `covering-sets.md`, but it's just trial division, no payoff. Not the
      direction. Do not resurrect it as "the answer."
    - **`p = 2ᵐ + qⁿ` is NOT an S-unit equation.** (S-unit eqn = fixed finite prime set S, solve
      `x+y=1` in S-units.) Here `q` is any prime and `p` is any prime — no fixed S. It's a
      de Polignac-type additive representation problem. Only `2ᵐ` is an S-unit.
    - **Scale:** dumps `/workspace/exploration/tmp/pk0.i64` (17,020,122 k=0 primes) and `kpos.i64`
      (82,979,878 k>0) are a PROTOTYPING slice — first 100M primes, max 2,038,074,659 (~2.04B).
      Real task dataset is much larger (primes approaching ~10¹²); deferred. Prototype on 2.04B to
      get the shape; reconfirm at scale later. This authoring container may not have the research
      warehouse mounted — rely on the `/workspace` dumps.
    
    ## Mechanism (what a "kill" is)
    Fix a prime `ℓ`; let `d = ord_ℓ(2)` (period of `2ᵐ mod ℓ`). For a prime `p`:
    - `p` is *killable by ℓ* iff `(p mod ℓ) ∈ ⟨2⟩ mod ℓ`. If `2ʳ ≡ p (mod ℓ)`, then
      `ℓ | p − 2ᵐ  ⇔  m ≡ r (mod d)`.
    - So `ℓ` kills the exponent progression `m ≡ r (mod d)` (one prime → a whole AP of exponents).
    For a k=0 prime, `ℓ | p − 2ᵐ` guarantees that position is a non-prime-power composite (if it
    were `ℓ` or `ℓ^k` the prime would be k>0). So killing an exponent = explaining that position.
    
    ## Question being measured
    What fraction of the 17,020,122 k=0 primes are **covering-explained** — every exponent
    `m` with `2ᵐ < p` is killed by some *small-order* prime `ℓ` — versus **accidental** (some
    exponent's only small factor comes from a large-order prime, i.e. the certificate tail)?
    This is the exponent-space **ceiling**: the most any covering system built from small-order
    primes could explain. It decides whether an elegant covering-system task is viable and what its
    honest coverage target is.
    
    Key contrast: certificate covers ~100% by allowing *any* prime `≤ √p_max` per exponent
    (unstructured, one prime patching one exponent). The covering system restricts to primes whose
    killed progressions *tile* the exponents. The gap between them = the accidental fraction.
    
    ## Core algorithm (per k=0 prime)
    Candidate set `C` = primes `ℓ` with `ord_ℓ(2) ≤ D_max`, value `≤ B_ℓ`.
    Precompute per `ℓ`: `d_ℓ = ord_ℓ(2)` and a map `sub[ℓ]: (residue mod ℓ) → r` over the `d_ℓ`
    subgroup elements `2ʳ mod ℓ`.
    ```
    for each k=0 prime p:
        L = floor(log2(p))                 # exponents m = 0..L with 2^m < p
        covered = 0                        # bitmask over m in [0, L]
        for ℓ in C:
            rem = p mod ℓ
            if rem in sub[ℓ]:
                r = sub[ℓ][rem]; d = d_ℓ
                for m = r, r+d, r+2d, ... <= L: set bit m in covered
        explained = (covered == (2^(L+1) - 1))    # every exponent killed
    fraction_explained = (# explained) / 17,020,122
    ```

    **Bleed (exp_cover on kpos.i64, full 82,979,878 k>0):**
    `D=64 → 0.00009% | 128 → 0.00017% | 256 → 0.00031% | 512 → 0.00050%` (416 primes at D=512).
    Certificate bleed = 0.0068%. So specificity (k0 cov / k>0 bleed) is best at SMALL D
    (~72,000:1 at D=512) and DEGRADES toward the certificate. The elegant end is the cleanest
    classifier. A k>0 prime bleeds only if its decomposition `q` is itself small-order AND all its
    other positions are covered — rare.
    
    **Anatomy of the holdouts (exp_char, bottleneck = argmax-order position):**
    - Exponent `m`: NO strong pattern. Bottleneck spread ~uniformly across exponents; top exponent
      `m=L` only 2.25% (mildly disfavored). The accidental position is not "the smallest difference."
    - `x = p−2^m`: STRONG pattern. Semiprime 88.6% (ω=3: 10.7%; never prime — confirms k=0), and
      **never has a factor ≤ 7, rarely ≤ 100** (smallest factor usually in (1000, 45000]). The
      holdout `x` is ROUGH — no small prime factor ⇒ no small-ORDER factor ⇒ no elegant covering
      catches it. Roughness = the accidental obstruction.
    
    **Unifying quantity: `needD(p)`** = smallest order cap that certifies p. Stratifies k=0 into
    structural (low order, genuine covering, ~1–11%) vs accidental (high order, rough-semiprime
    position, = certificate tail). Certificate = covering with D unbounded. This is the real
    characterization; the "two approaches" were one object read at two ends of the order axis.
    Artifacts: `exp_cover.cc` (wide-D + kpos bleed), `exp_char.cc` (needD + anatomy).

    1. **Ceiling curve:** fraction explained vs `D_max` (2,4,8,12,24,48,100,…) and vs `B_ℓ`. ✓ done above.
    2. **Structure:** among explained primes, which `(r mod d, ℓ)` recur — does a compact universal

    3. **Gap to certificate:** certificate ≈ 100%; covering-system = X%. `100 − X` = accidental
       fraction. This is the honest cost of elegance.
    4. (secondary) **Minimal system:** smallest small-order `ℓ`-set explaining the largest fraction.
    
    ## Implementation notes
    - Native C++, multithreaded, streaming over `pk0.i64` (reuse `cert_minimize.cc` /

    - Cost: 17M primes × |C| candidates × O(1) lookup. Small |C| for small `D_max` → seconds–min.
    - Memory bounded: candidate maps are `Σ d_ℓ`; per-prime bitmask ≤ ~40 bits.

    ## What the result decides
    - **High explained fraction** → an exponent-space covering-system task is viable; reframe the

    - **Low fraction (few %)** → confirms most k=0 primes are accidental; the covering system is a
      genuine but partial result. Decide whether that's the task, or whether to combine approaches.
    - Either way the OUTPUT (covering systems + certified primes) is the payoff — unlike the
      certificate.
    
    ## Proof-direction nuance (for the eventual task, not the measurement)
    On known-k=0 primes, `ℓ | p − 2ᵐ` suffices to explain a position. To *prove* `p` is k=0 a

    Below is (1) a synthesis of your notes into one chain of necessary conditions for the only surviving case, (2) the single decision procedure that chain implies, and (3) a FLINT program that runs exactly that procedure — nothing else — to exhaustion for `p < 10^256`, reporting for every candidate *which* condition of the chain kills it.
    
    ---
    
    ## 1. The reduced problem
    
    Let `p` prime, `p = 2^m1 + q^n1 = 2^m2 + q^n2`, `q` odd prime, `m1 > m2 ≥ 1`, `n2 > n1 ≥ 1`, `Δm = m1−m2`, `Δn = n2−n1`, and
    
    ```
    A := (2^Δm − 1)/q^n1 = (q^Δn − 1)/2^m2,        A·p = 2^Δm·q^Δn − 1 .
    ```
    
    What is already closed (I re-checked each step):
    
    | case | closed by | status |
    |---|---|---|
    | `Δm` odd | mod-3 alternation (§1 of the notes; needs only `p > 3`) | closed |
    | `Δm` even, `Δn` even | `Ap = X²−1` with `A < X/√6` (§6.2 + §6.4, `d = 2`) | closed (the bare `A < X` of the older note is *not* enough — `A = X−1, p = X+1` must be excluded, and √6 does it) |
    | `A = 1` | `2^Δm−1 = q^n1`, `q^Δn−1 = 2^m2`: elementary Catalan-type splitting gives `q = 3, Δm = 2, Δn = 1, m2 = 1`, i.e. `p = 11` | closed |
    
    So the **whole problem is**: `Δm = 2k` even, `Δn` odd, `A > 1`, `q` odd prime, `p` prime. Everything below assumes exactly that.
    
    ## 2. The chain of necessary conditions (synthesis)
    
    All of these are proved in your notes; I list them in the order a decision procedure should apply them, with the sections they come from, and I note two places where they sharpen each other.
    
    **(N0) Determination.** `n1 = v_q(2^Δm−1)`, `A` = q-free part of `2^Δm−1`, `m2 = v2(q−1)` (§5.1, §5.2). Hence a configuration is a pair `(q, Δm)` with `q | 2^Δm−1`, and `Δn` is the unique odd integer with `q^Δn = A·2^m2 + 1` — if it exists (§5.3).
    
    **(N1) Size.** `Δn ≥ 3`, hence `q³ ≤ q^Δn < 2^Δm`, hence `Δm ≥ 6` (§9.3, §9.4). `m2 = v2(q−1) ≤ k` (E3). `q^n1` divides exactly one of `2^k ∓ 1`, so `q^n1 ≤ 2^k+1` and `A ≥ 2^k−1` (§5.6).
    
    **(N2) Window.** `2^m2(2^k−1) < q^Δn < 2^2k` (E4, §9.3, §9.5). For `q > 2^{2k/5}` this forces `Δn = 3`, for `q > 2^{k/2}` it forces `n1 = 1`.
    
    **(N3) Mod 3.** `q = 3` or `q ≡ 1 (mod 3)` (§1).
    
    **(N4) Legendre parity.** `(q/p) = 1` resolves to: `q ≡ 3 (8) ⇒ n1 odd`; `q ≡ 7 (8) ⇒ n1 even`, so `q² | 2^Δm−1`; `q ≡ 1 (4)` gives nothing (§4, §7.1, §7.2).
    
    **(N5) Order condition on `q−1`.** With `u` the odd part of `q−1`: `u | 2^Δm−1`, i.e. `ord_ℓ(2) | Δm` for every odd prime `ℓ | q−1` (§8.2).
    
    **(N6) Exact valuation identity.** For every odd prime `ℓ | q−1`: `v_ℓ(Δn) = v_ℓ(2^Δm−1) − v_ℓ(q−1)` (§8.3). *Sharpening:* the right-hand side is a function of `(q, Δm)` alone, so `v_ℓ(q−1) > v_ℓ(2^Δm−1)` kills the pair before `Δn` is even considered, and otherwise pins the exact `ℓ`-adic valuation of `Δn`. This subsumes (N5) (`ℓ ∤ 2^Δm−1` is the case RHS `< 0`).
    
    **(N7) Odd-order closure.** For every prime `ℓ | 2^Δm−1`, `ℓ ≠ q`: `ord_ℓ(q)` is odd and `ord_ℓ(q) | Δn`; more precisely `ord_{ℓ^e}(q) | Δn` for `ℓ^e ∥ 2^Δm−1` (§5.4, §10.2). Equivalently `ord_A(q) | Δn`. (N3) is the instance `ℓ = 3`.
    
    **(N8) gcd.** `d = gcd(Δm, Δn)` is odd and not divisible by 3 (§6.4–§6.6); for any prime `r | d`, `p ≡ 1 (mod r)` (C2).
    
    **(N9) Exact test.** `q^Δn = A·2^m2 + 1` (§5.3).
    
    Two remarks that matter for the *search*:
    
    * (N0)–(N8) are all functions of `(q, Δm)` plus, for the last ones, a short list of admissible `Δn` (odd multiples of `lcm(L, ∏ ℓ^{t_ℓ})` inside the window of (N2)). None of them needs the cofactor `A` built, and none needs `2^Δm−1` factored — only its *known* small prime factors, which we get for free (below).
    * The only thing that needs `2^Δm−1` "factored" is *enumerating* `q`. That is what made the §5.3 procedure stall at `Δm ≈ 30` in your table. The fix: split the candidate space by the size of `q`.
    
    ## 3. The decision procedure
    
    Fix `M = ⌊256·log₂10⌋ = 850` (so `m1 ≤ M`) and a threshold `Q` (default `2^32`).
    
    **Stage S (`q ≤ Q`).** Every solution with `q ≤ Q` has `ord_q(2) | Δm ≤ M−1`. So scan all primes `q ≤ Q`, compute `ord_q(2)` (factor `q−1` with `n_factor`), keep those with order `≤ M−1`. This list is simultaneously (a) the complete candidate list for Stage S and (b) the complete list of primes `ℓ ≤ Q` dividing any `2^Δm−1`, i.e. the "known prime support" needed for (N7). For each candidate `q` and each even `Δm` in `ord_q(2)·ℤ` with `m2+Δm ≤ M`, run the cascade (N1)→(N9) and record the first condition that fails. This is §5.3 + §8 + §9 + §10 run to `Δm = 849`, with no factoring.
    
    **Stage L (`q > Q`).** Here `n2 = n1 + Δn` is tiny: `Q^n2 < q^n2 ≤ 1.5·(2^m1 − 2^m2)` gives `n2 ≤ (m1+0.585)/log₂Q ≤ 26`, while (N1) gives `n2 ≥ 4` and `n2 > 3(m1−1)/Δm`. For fixed `(Δm, m2, n2)` the base is forced: `N < q^n2 ≤ 1.5N` has the unique integer solution `q = ⌈N^{1/n2}⌉`, so one `fmpz_root` per triple decides it (`q^n2 − N` must be a pure power `q^n1`). Roughly `2·10^6` roots for `M = 850`.
    
    Together the two stages exhaust all `p < 10^256` in the even/odd case, and Stage S additionally tells you *why* each `(q, Δm)` dies. The program also runs the raw §5.3 one-shot test ("oracle") on every Stage-S pair independently of the filters and aborts loudly if a filter ever contradicts it, so a mistake in any filter cannot silently lose a solution.
    
    ## 4. The program
    
    ```cpp
    // evenodd.cpp
    //
    // The Δm even / Δn odd / A > 1 case of   p = 2^m1 + q^n1 = 2^m2 + q^n2   (q odd prime, p prime),
    // run to exhaustion for p < 10^D as one decision procedure with the filter chain
    //   (N1) size   (N3) mod 3   (N4) Legendre parity   (N5/N6) q-1 order & valuation identity
    //   (N7) odd-order closure   (N2,N6,N8) window on Δn   (N9) exact test.
    //
    // Build:  g++ -O3 -march=native -std=c++17 -pthread evenodd.cpp -lflint -lgmp -o evenodd
    // Run:    ./evenodd --digits 256 [--qbits 32] [--threads 24] [--csv out.csv] [--no-table] [--selftest]
    //
    // Stage S  (q <= 2^qbits):  §5.3 decision procedure on (q, Δm), with q enumerated by ord_q(2) <= Mmax-1
    //                           (no factoring of 2^Δm-1), and the cascade of necessary conditions applied in order.
    // Stage L  (q >  2^qbits):  n2 = n1+Δn <= (m1+0.585)/qbits, q forced as ceil((2^m1-2^m2)^(1/n2)); one root per triple.
    
    #include <flint/flint.h>
    #include <flint/fmpz.h>
    #include <flint/ulong_extras.h>
    
    #include <cstdio>
    #include <cstdlib>
    #include <cstring>
    #include <cmath>
    #include <cstdint>
    #include <vector>
    #include <string>
    #include <thread>
    #include <atomic>
    #include <mutex>
    #include <algorithm>
    #include <chrono>
    
    typedef unsigned __int128 u128;
    
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ configuration
    
    struct Cfg {
        int digits = 256;
        int Mmax = 0;            // m1 <= Mmax  (derived from digits unless --mmax)
        int threads = 0;
        int qbits = 32;          // Stage S covers q <= 2^qbits
        ulong Q = 0;
        bool table = true;
        bool selftest = false;
        const char* csv = nullptr;
    };
    static Cfg cfg;
    
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ the filter chain
    
    enum Kill { K_NONE = 0, K_SIZE, K_M2, K_MOD3, K_PARITY, K_ORDU, K_VAL, K_CLOSURE, K_WINDOW, K_EXACT, K_HIT, K_COUNT };
    static const char* KSHORT[K_COUNT] = { "-", "size", "m2>k", "mod3", "par", "ordu", "val", "clos", "win", "exact", "HIT" };
    static const char* KLONG[K_COUNT] = {
        "-",
        "N1  q^3 >= 2^Dm                      (Dn>=3 and q^Dn < 2^Dm, §9.3/§9.4)",
        "N1  m2 = v2(q-1) > Dm/2                                   (E3)",
        "N3  q != 3 and q != 1 (mod 3)                  (§1 = §5.4 at l=3)",
        "N4  parity of n1 = v_q(2^Dm-1) contradicts (q/p)=1     (§4, §7.1)",
        "N5  odd l | q-1 with ord_l(2) not dividing Dm  (u | 2^Dm-1, §8.2)",
        "N6  v_l(2^Dm-1) < v_l(q-1) for an odd l | q-1      (identity §8.3)",
        "N7  ord_l(q) even for a prime l | 2^Dm-1, l != q        (§5.4)",
        "N2  no odd Dn: L|Dn, v_l(Dn)=t_l, 3 nmid gcd, (C2), window (§9.5,§10,§6)",
        "N9  admissible Dn exist but q^Dn != A*2^m2 + 1           (§5.3)",
        "HIT"
    };
    
    struct Cand {                 // prime q <= Q with ord_q(2) <= Mmax-1
        ulong q, e, u;            // e = ord_q(2), u = odd part of q-1
        int m2;                   // v2(q-1)
        n_factor_t f;             // factorisation of q-1
    };
    static std::vector<Cand> g_cands;                 // sorted by q
    static std::vector<std::vector<int>> g_byord;     // g_byord[d] = indices with ord_q(2) == d
    
    struct PairRes {
        int Dm, n1, m2, nadm;
        ulong q, wit, L, mult, Dn;
        ulong abits;
        Kill kill;
        bool oracle;
    };
    
    struct Hit { std::string src, p, q, A; int m1, m2, n1, n2; };
    static std::mutex g_mu;
    static std::vector<Hit> g_hits;
    static std::atomic<int> g_unsound{0};
    
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
    
    static std::string zstr(const fmpz_t x) {
        char* s = fmpz_get_str(NULL, 10, x);
        std::string r(s);
        flint_free(s);
        return r;
    }
    
    static const ulong CAP = (1ULL << 40);
    static ulong lcm_cap(ulong a, ulong b) {
        if (a >= CAP || b >= CAP) return CAP;
        ulong g = n_gcd(a, b);
        u128 l = (u128)(a / g) * b;
        return l >= CAP ? CAP : (ulong)l;
    }
    static ulong pow_cap(ulong l, int t) {
        u128 r = 1;
        for (int i = 0; i < t; ++i) { r *= l; if (r >= CAP) return CAP; }
        return (ulong)r;
    }
    
    // multiplicative order of a modulo the prime n, given the factorisation f of n-1
    static ulong mult_order(ulong a, ulong n, const n_factor_t* f) {
        a %= n;
        ulong o = n - 1;
        for (int i = 0; i < f->num; ++i) {
            ulong r = f->p[i];
            for (int j = 0; j < f->exp[i]; ++j) {
                if (o % r == 0 && n_powmod2(a, (slong)(o / r), n) == 1) o /= r; else break;
            }
        }
        return o;
    }
    
    static void record_hit(const char* src, int m1, int m2, int n1, int n2, const fmpz_t q, const fmpz_t p, const fmpz_t A) {
        Hit h; h.src = src; h.m1 = m1; h.m2 = m2; h.n1 = n1; h.n2 = n2;
        h.p = zstr(p); h.q = zstr(q); h.A = zstr(A);
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_mu);
        g_hits.push_back(h);
        std::printf("!!! HIT [%s]  p=%s  q=%s  m1=%d m2=%d n1=%d n2=%d  A=%s\n", src, h.p.c_str(), h.q.c_str(), m1, m2, n1, n2, h.A.c_str());
        std::fflush(stdout);
    }
    
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ Stage S: candidate scan
    
    static void scan_worker(std::atomic<ulong>& next, ulong chunk, std::vector<Cand>& out) {
        n_primes_t it;
        n_primes_init(it);
        const ulong Dmax = (ulong)(cfg.Mmax - 1);
        for (;;) {
            ulong lo = next.fetch_add(chunk);
            if (lo > cfg.Q) break;
            ulong hi = std::min<ulong>(cfg.Q, lo + chunk - 1);
            n_primes_jump(it, lo);
            ulong q;
            while ((q = n_primes_next(it)) <= hi) {
                if (q < 3) continue;
                Cand c; c.q = q;
                n_factor_init(&c.f);
                n_factor(&c.f, q - 1, 0);
                c.e = mult_order(2 % q, q, &c.f);
                if (c.e > Dmax) continue;
                c.m2 = __builtin_ctzll(q - 1);
                c.u = (q - 1) >> c.m2;
                out.push_back(c);
            }
        }
        n_primes_clear(it);
        flint_cleanup();
    }
    
    static void stageS_scan(int threads) {
        std::atomic<ulong> next{3};
        ulong chunk = 1ULL << 22;
        std::vector<std::vector<Cand>> outs(threads);
        std::vector<std::thread> th;
        for (int t = 0; t < threads; ++t) th.emplace_back(scan_worker, std::ref(next), chunk, std::ref(outs[t]));
        for (auto& x : th) x.join();
        for (auto& v : outs) g_cands.insert(g_cands.end(), v.begin(), v.end());
        std::sort(g_cands.begin(), g_cands.end(), [](const Cand& a, const Cand& b) { return a.q < b.q; });
        g_byord.assign(cfg.Mmax + 1, {});
        for (int i = 0; i < (int)g_cands.size(); ++i) g_byord[g_cands[i].e].push_back(i);
    }
    
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ Stage S: the cascade on one pair (q, Δm)
    
    static PairRes eval_pair(const Cand& c, int Dm) {
        PairRes R{}; R.Dm = Dm; R.q = c.q; R.m2 = c.m2; R.kill = K_NONE;
        const ulong q = c.q;
        const int k = Dm / 2;
    
        fmpz_t M, A, X, T, Qn, lo, hi, qz, lz, pz;
        fmpz_init(M); fmpz_init(A); fmpz_init(X); fmpz_init(T); fmpz_init(Qn);
        fmpz_init(lo); fmpz_init(hi); fmpz_init(qz); fmpz_init(lz); fmpz_init(pz);
    
        // (N0)  M = 2^Dm - 1,  n1 = v_q(M),  A = M / q^n1,  X = A*2^m2 + 1
        fmpz_one(M); fmpz_mul_2exp(M, M, Dm); fmpz_sub_ui(M, M, 1);
        fmpz_set_ui(qz, q);
        R.n1 = (int)fmpz_remove(A, M, qz);
        R.abits = fmpz_bits(A);
        fmpz_mul_2exp(X, A, c.m2); fmpz_add_ui(X, X, 1);
    
        // oracle: the bare §5.3 test, independent of every filter below
        { slong ex = fmpz_remove(T, X, qz); R.oracle = (ex >= 1 && (ex & 1) && fmpz_is_one(T)); }
    
        std::vector<std::pair<ulong, int>> valreq;   // (l, t_l): required v_l(Dn)
        ulong mult = 1, L = 1;
    
        for (;;) {
            // (N1) size
            if (Dm < 96 && (u128)q * q * q >= ((u128)1 << Dm)) { R.kill = K_SIZE; break; }
            if (c.m2 > k) { R.kill = K_M2; break; }
            // (N3) mod 3
            if (q != 3 && q % 3 != 1) { R.kill = K_MOD3; break; }
            // (N4) Legendre parity of n1
            { ulong r8 = q & 7;
              if ((r8 == 3 && (R.n1 & 1) == 0) || (r8 == 7 && (R.n1 & 1) == 1)) { R.kill = K_PARITY; break; } }
            // (N5)+(N6) for odd l | q-1 :  a_l = v_l(M) >= v_l(q-1),  t_l = a_l - v_l(q-1) = v_l(Dn)
            bool dead = false;
            for (int i = 0; i < c.f.num && !dead; ++i) {
                ulong l = c.f.p[i];
                if (l == 2) continue;
                fmpz_set_ui(lz, l);
                slong a = fmpz_remove(T, M, lz);
                if (a == 0) { R.kill = K_ORDU; R.wit = l; dead = true; break; }
                int t = (int)a - c.f.exp[i];
                if (t < 0) { R.kill = K_VAL; R.wit = l; dead = true; break; }
                valreq.push_back({l, t});
                mult = lcm_cap(mult, pow_cap(l, t));
            }
            if (dead) break;
            // (N7) odd-order closure on the known primes l | 2^Dm - 1  (l <= Q, l != q, l nmid q-1)
            for (int d = 1; d <= Dm && !dead; ++d) {
                if (Dm % d) continue;
                for (int idx : g_byord[d]) {
                    const Cand& cl = g_cands[idx];
                    ulong l = cl.q;
                    if (l == q || (q - 1) % l == 0) continue;
                    ulong o = mult_order(q % l, l, &cl.f);
                    if ((o & 1) == 0) { R.kill = K_CLOSURE; R.wit = l; dead = true; break; }
                    fmpz_set_ui(lz, l);
                    slong al = fmpz_remove(T, M, lz);          // l^al || 2^Dm - 1
                    if (al >= 2) {                              // refine to ord_{l^al}(q) when it fits a word
                        u128 le = 1; for (slong j = 0; j < al; ++j) le *= l;
                        if (le < ((u128)1 << 62)) {
                            ulong lev = (ulong)le, o2 = o, qm = q % lev;
                            while (n_powmod2(qm, (slong)o2, lev) != 1) o2 *= l;
                            o = o2;
                        }
                    }
                    L = lcm_cap(L, o);
                }
            }
            if (dead) break;
            R.L = L;
            mult = lcm_cap(mult, L);
            R.mult = mult;
            // (N2)+(N6)+(N8) admissible Dn:  odd multiples of mult, exact valuations, 3 nmid gcd, (C2), window
            fmpz_one(lo); fmpz_mul_2exp(lo, lo, k); fmpz_sub_ui(lo, lo, 1); fmpz_mul_2exp(lo, lo, c.m2);   // 2^m2 (2^k - 1)
            fmpz_one(hi); fmpz_mul_2exp(hi, hi, Dm);                                                       // 2^Dm
            std::vector<ulong> adm;
            if (mult & 1) {
                for (ulong Dn = mult; Dn <= (ulong)Dm; Dn += 2 * mult) {
                    if (Dn < 3) continue;
                    if (Dm % 3 == 0 && Dn % 3 == 0) continue;                       // §6.6
                    bool ok = true;
                    for (auto& pr : valreq) { ulong x = Dn; int v = n_remove(&x, pr.first); if (v != pr.second) { ok = false; break; } }
                    if (!ok) continue;
                    fmpz_pow_ui(Qn, qz, Dn);
                    if (fmpz_cmp(Qn, lo) <= 0) continue;
                    if (fmpz_cmp(Qn, hi) >= 0) break;
                    ulong g = n_gcd((ulong)Dm, Dn);
                    if (g > 1) {                                                     // (C2): p = 1 (mod r) for r | gcd
                        fmpz_pow_ui(pz, qz, (ulong)R.n1 + Dn);
                        fmpz_one(T); fmpz_mul_2exp(T, T, c.m2); fmpz_add(pz, pz, T);
                        n_factor_t fg; n_factor_init(&fg); n_factor(&fg, g, 0);
                        bool c2 = true;
                        for (int i = 0; i < fg.num; ++i) if (fmpz_fdiv_ui(pz, fg.p[i]) != 1) { c2 = false; break; }
                        if (!c2) continue;
                    }
                    adm.push_back(Dn);
                }
            }
            R.nadm = (int)adm.size();
            if (adm.empty()) { R.kill = K_WINDOW; break; }
            // (N9) exact
            for (ulong Dn : adm) {
                fmpz_pow_ui(Qn, qz, Dn);
                if (fmpz_equal(Qn, X)) {
                    R.kill = K_HIT; R.Dn = Dn;
                    int m1 = c.m2 + Dm, n2 = R.n1 + (int)Dn;
                    fmpz_pow_ui(pz, qz, (ulong)n2); fmpz_one(T); fmpz_mul_2exp(T, T, c.m2); fmpz_add(pz, pz, T);
                    record_hit("S", m1, c.m2, R.n1, n2, qz, pz, A);
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (R.kill != K_HIT) R.kill = K_EXACT;
            break;
        }
    
        if (R.oracle != (R.kill == K_HIT)) {
            g_unsound++;
            std::printf("*** FILTER/ORACLE DISAGREEMENT at q=%lu Dm=%d: oracle=%d cascade=%s\n", q, Dm, (int)R.oracle, KSHORT[R.kill]);
        }
    
        fmpz_clear(M); fmpz_clear(A); fmpz_clear(X); fmpz_clear(T); fmpz_clear(Qn);
        fmpz_clear(lo); fmpz_clear(hi); fmpz_clear(qz); fmpz_clear(lz); fmpz_clear(pz);
        return R;
    }
    
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ Stage L: forced-q roots for q > Q
    
    struct LStat { uint64_t triples = 0, divisors = 0, hits = 0; };
    
    static void large_worker(std::atomic<int>& next, std::vector<LStat>& st, std::atomic<int>& done) {
        fmpz_t N, r, q, P, R, T, A, p, two;
        fmpz_init(N); fmpz_init(r); fmpz_init(q); fmpz_init(P); fmpz_init(R); fmpz_init(T); fmpz_init(A); fmpz_init(p); fmpz_init(two);
        fmpz_set_ui(two, 2);
        const double log2Q = (double)cfg.qbits;
        for (;;) {
            int Dm = next.fetch_add(2);
            if (Dm > cfg.Mmax - 1) break;
            int k = Dm / 2;
            for (int m2 = 1; m2 <= k && m2 + Dm <= cfg.Mmax; ++m2) {
                int m1 = m2 + Dm;
                int n2lo = std::max(4, (3 * (m1 - 1)) / Dm + 1);            // n1>=1, Dn>=3, q^3 < 2^Dm
                int n2hi = (int)std::floor((m1 + 0.585) / log2Q);            // q > Q  =>  n2 < (m1 + log2 1.5)/log2 Q
                if (n2hi < n2lo) continue;
                fmpz_one(N); fmpz_mul_2exp(N, N, m1);
                fmpz_one(T); fmpz_mul_2exp(T, T, m2);
                fmpz_sub(N, N, T);                                            // N = 2^m1 - 2^m2
                for (int n2 = n2lo; n2 <= n2hi; ++n2) {
                    st[Dm].triples++;
                    (void)fmpz_root(r, N, n2);                                // floor root
                    fmpz_add_ui(q, r, 1);                                     // the unique q with N < q^n2 <= 1.5N
                    fmpz_pow_ui(P, q, n2);
                    fmpz_sub(R, P, N);                                        // must equal q^n1
                    if (fmpz_cmp(R, q) >= 0) {
                        slong e = fmpz_remove(T, R, q);
                        if (e >= 1 && fmpz_is_one(T)) {
                            st[Dm].hits++;
                            fmpz_one(T); fmpz_mul_2exp(T, T, m2); fmpz_add(p, P, T);
                            fmpz_one(A); fmpz_mul_2exp(A, A, Dm); fmpz_sub_ui(A, A, 1);
                            fmpz_pow_ui(T, q, e); fmpz_divexact(A, A, T);
                            record_hit("L", m1, m2, (int)e, n2, q, p, A);
                        }
                    }
                    if (fmpz_is_odd(q)) {                                     // structural note: does q | 2^Dm - 1 at all?
                        fmpz_powm_ui(T, two, Dm, q);
                        if (fmpz_is_one(T)) {
                            st[Dm].divisors++;
                            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_mu);
                            fmpz_sub_ui(T, q, 1);
                            std::printf("  [L] Dm=%d m2=%d n2=%d: forced q (%lu bits) divides 2^Dm-1; v2(q-1)=%lu, prime=%d, exact=no\n",
                                        Dm, m2, n2, (ulong)fmpz_bits(q), (ulong)fmpz_val2(T), fmpz_is_probabprime(q));
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            int d = done.fetch_add(1) + 1;
            if (d % 50 == 0) std::fprintf(stderr, "  stage L: %d even Dm done\n", d);
        }
        fmpz_clear(N); fmpz_clear(r); fmpz_clear(q); fmpz_clear(P); fmpz_clear(R); fmpz_clear(T); fmpz_clear(A); fmpz_clear(p); fmpz_clear(two);
        flint_cleanup();
    }
    
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ self-test of the forced-q machinery (all parities, small range)
    
    static void selftest() {
        std::printf("=== self-test: all integer solutions of 2^m1 + q^n1 = 2^m2 + q^n2 with m1 <= 60 (any parity, q odd) ===\n");
        fmpz_t N, r, q, P, R, T;
        fmpz_init(N); fmpz_init(r); fmpz_init(q); fmpz_init(P); fmpz_init(R); fmpz_init(T);
        int found = 0;
        for (int m1 = 2; m1 <= 60; ++m1)
            for (int m2 = 1; m2 < m1; ++m2) {
                fmpz_one(N); fmpz_mul_2exp(N, N, m1); fmpz_one(T); fmpz_mul_2exp(T, T, m2); fmpz_sub(N, N, T);
                for (int n2 = 2; n2 < m1; ++n2) {
                    (void)fmpz_root(r, N, n2); fmpz_add_ui(q, r, 1);
                    if (!fmpz_is_odd(q)) continue;
                    fmpz_pow_ui(P, q, n2); fmpz_sub(R, P, N);
                    if (fmpz_cmp(R, q) < 0) continue;
                    slong e = fmpz_remove(T, R, q);
                    if (e >= 1 && fmpz_is_one(T)) {
                        fmpz_one(T); fmpz_mul_2exp(T, T, m2); fmpz_add(T, P, T);
                        std::printf("  p=%s = 2^%d + %s^%ld = 2^%d + %s^%d   (Dm=%d, Dn=%d, p prime: %d)\n",
                                    zstr(T).c_str(), m1, zstr(q).c_str(), (long)e, m2, zstr(q).c_str(), n2, m1 - m2, n2 - (int)e, fmpz_is_prime(T));
                        ++found;
                    }
                }
            }
        std::printf("  expected exactly: 11 (A=1), 35 (A=1), 133 (A=3, Dn even, composite). found %d.\n\n", found);
        fmpz_clear(N); fmpz_clear(r); fmpz_clear(q); fmpz_clear(P); fmpz_clear(R); fmpz_clear(T);
    }
    
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ main
    
    int main(int argc, char** argv) {
        for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {
            auto need = [&](const char* n) { if (i + 1 >= argc) { std::fprintf(stderr, "%s needs a value\n", n); std::exit(1); } return argv[++i]; };
            if (!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--digits")) cfg.digits = std::atoi(need("--digits"));
            else if (!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--mmax")) cfg.Mmax = std::atoi(need("--mmax"));
            else if (!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--threads")) cfg.threads = std::atoi(need("--threads"));
            else if (!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--qbits")) cfg.qbits = std::atoi(need("--qbits"));
            else if (!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--no-table")) cfg.table = false;
            else if (!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--selftest")) cfg.selftest = true;
            else if (!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--csv")) cfg.csv = need("--csv");
            else { std::fprintf(stderr, "unknown option %s\n", argv[i]); return 1; }
        }
        if (cfg.Mmax <= 0) cfg.Mmax = (int)std::floor(cfg.digits * std::log2(10.0));
        if (cfg.qbits < 20 || cfg.qbits > 40) { std::fprintf(stderr, "--qbits must be in [20,40]\n"); return 1; }
        cfg.Q = (1ULL << cfg.qbits);
        int threads = cfg.threads > 0 ? cfg.threads : (int)std::thread::hardware_concurrency();
        if (threads <= 0) threads = 1;
    
        std::printf("evenodd: p = 2^m1 + q^n1 = 2^m2 + q^n2,  p < 10^%d  (m1 <= %d),  case Dm even / Dn odd / A > 1,  %d threads\n",
                    cfg.digits, cfg.Mmax, threads);
        std::printf("Stage S: q <= 2^%d via ord_q(2) <= %d;  Stage L: q > 2^%d via forced roots, n2 <= (m1+0.585)/%d.\n\n",
                    cfg.qbits, cfg.Mmax - 1, cfg.qbits, cfg.qbits);
    
        if (cfg.selftest) selftest();
    
        // ---------------- Stage S
        auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        std::fprintf(stderr, "stage S: scanning primes q <= 2^%d for ord_q(2) <= %d ...\n", cfg.qbits, cfg.Mmax - 1);
        stageS_scan(threads);
        double tscan = std::chrono::duration<double>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now()-t0).count();
        std::printf("Stage S candidate primes (q <= 2^%d, ord_q(2) <= %d): %zu   [%.1f s]\n", cfg.qbits, cfg.Mmax - 1, g_cands.size(), tscan);
    
        std::vector<std::vector<PairRes>> byDm(cfg.Mmax + 1);
        uint64_t kills[K_COUNT] = {0};
        uint64_t pairs = 0;
        for (const Cand& c : g_cands) {
            for (ulong Dm = c.e; Dm + (ulong)c.m2 <= (ulong)cfg.Mmax; Dm += c.e) {
                if (Dm & 1) continue;          // Dm even (mod-3 argument); odd multiples of an odd order never qualify
                if (Dm < 4) continue;          // Dm = 2 is the A = 1 configuration (p = 11), excluded
                PairRes R = eval_pair(c, (int)Dm);
                byDm[Dm].push_back(R);
                kills[R.kill]++;
                ++pairs;
            }
        }
        double tS = std::chrono::duration<double>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now()-t0).count();
    
        std::printf("\n=== Stage S: %llu pairs (q, Dm) with q | 2^Dm - 1, q <= 2^%d, 4 <= Dm <= %d even   [%.1f s] ===\n",
                    (unsigned long long)pairs, cfg.qbits, cfg.Mmax - 1, tS);
        std::printf("First failing condition in the chain (cascade, not marginals):\n");
        {
            uint64_t surv = pairs;
            for (int kk = K_SIZE; kk < K_COUNT; ++kk) {
                std::printf("  %-72s  kills %7llu   survivors %7llu\n", KLONG[kk], (unsigned long long)kills[kk],
                            (unsigned long long)(kk == K_HIT ? kills[K_HIT] : (surv -= kills[kk])));
            }
        }
        if (g_unsound) std::printf("*** %d filter/oracle disagreements — a filter is unsound, fix before trusting.\n", g_unsound.load());
        else std::printf("  oracle (bare §5.3 test on every pair) agrees with the cascade on all %llu pairs.\n", (unsigned long long)pairs);
    
        if (cfg.table) {
            std::printf("\nPer-Dm table: q[n1,m2,A~2^bits]:first-kill(witness)   {L = lcm of known odd orders, #adm = admissible Dn}\n");
            for (int Dm = 4; Dm <= cfg.Mmax; ++Dm) {
                if (byDm[Dm].empty()) continue;
                std::printf("Dm=%4d k=%3d |", Dm, Dm / 2);
                for (const PairRes& R : byDm[Dm]) {
                    std::printf(" %lu[%d,%d,%lu]:%s", R.q, R.n1, R.m2, R.abits, KSHORT[R.kill]);
                    if (R.kill == K_ORDU || R.kill == K_VAL || R.kill == K_CLOSURE) std::printf("(l=%lu)", R.wit);
                    if (R.kill == K_WINDOW) std::printf("(L=%lu)", R.L);
                    if (R.kill == K_EXACT) std::printf("(#adm=%d)", R.nadm);
                }
                std::printf("\n");
            }
        }
    
        // ---------------- Stage L
        t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        std::vector<LStat> lst(cfg.Mmax + 1);
        {
            std::atomic<int> next{6}, done{0};
            std::vector<std::thread> th;
            for (int t = 0; t < threads; ++t) th.emplace_back(large_worker, std::ref(next), std::ref(lst), std::ref(done));
            for (auto& x : th) x.join();
        }
        double tL = std::chrono::duration<double>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now()-t0).count();
        uint64_t Ltr = 0, Ldiv = 0, Lhit = 0;
        for (int Dm = 6; Dm <= cfg.Mmax; ++Dm) { Ltr += lst[Dm].triples; Ldiv += lst[Dm].divisors; Lhit += lst[Dm].hits; }
        std::printf("\n=== Stage L: q > 2^%d, forced q = ceil((2^m1-2^m2)^(1/n2)),  6 <= Dm even, 1 <= m2 <= min(k, %d-Dm),  4 <= n2 <= (m1+0.585)/%d   [%.1f s] ===\n",
                    cfg.qbits, cfg.Mmax, cfg.qbits, tL);
        std::printf("  triples (Dm,m2,n2): %llu   forced q dividing 2^Dm-1: %llu   exact solutions: %llu\n",
                    (unsigned long long)Ltr, (unsigned long long)Ldiv, (unsigned long long)Lhit);
    
        // ---------------- CSV
        if (cfg.csv) {
            FILE* f = std::fopen(cfg.csv, "w");
            if (f) {
                std::fprintf(f, "Dm,S_pairs,size,m2,mod3,par,ordu,val,clos,win,exact,S_hits,L_triples,L_divisors,L_hits\n");
                for (int Dm = 4; Dm <= cfg.Mmax; ++Dm) {
                    if (byDm[Dm].empty() && lst[Dm].triples == 0) continue;
                    uint64_t kc[K_COUNT] = {0};
                    for (auto& R : byDm[Dm]) kc[R.kill]++;
                    std::fprintf(f, "%d,%zu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu,%llu\n", Dm, byDm[Dm].size(),
                                 (unsigned long long)kc[K_SIZE], (unsigned long long)kc[K_M2], (unsigned long long)kc[K_MOD3],
                                 (unsigned long long)kc[K_PARITY], (unsigned long long)kc[K_ORDU], (unsigned long long)kc[K_VAL],

                                 (unsigned long long)lst[Dm].hits);

        // ---------------- verdict
        std::printf("\n=== Result ===\n");
        if (g_hits.empty()) {

                        "A = 1 => p = 11) this exhausts the range.\n", cfg.digits, cfg.Mmax);
        } else {

            fmpz_t p, q;
            fmpz_init(p); fmpz_init(q);
            for (auto& h : g_hits) {

                std::printf("  [%s] p=%s (%zu digits) q=%s m1=%d m2=%d n1=%d n2=%d A=%s  p prime: %d  q prime: %d\n",
                            h.src.c_str(), h.p.c_str(), h.p.size(), h.q.c_str(), h.m1, h.m2, h.n1, h.n2, h.A.c_str(),
                            fmpz_is_prime(p), fmpz_is_prime(q));
            }
            fmpz_clear(p); fmpz_clear(q);
        }
        flint_cleanup();
        return 0;
    }

    What you get:
    
    * The Stage-S cascade summary — one line per condition of the chain, with kills and survivors *in sequence*, and a guarantee line from the oracle.
    * A per-`Δm` line in the style of your §5.3/§8.5/§9.7/§10.4 tables, extended to `Δm = 848`, e.g. `Dm=12 k=6 | 3[2,1,10]:clos(l=5) 5[1,2,10]:mod3 7[1,1,9]:par 13[1,2,8]:clos(l=5)` (with parity applied before closure, the `q = 7` row dies on §7.1 rather than `ℓ = 5`; both hold).
    * A Stage-L line certifying that for `q > 2^32` no forced base even divides `2^Δm−1`, let alone solves the equation.
    * `--selftest` exercises the forced-root machinery on all parities and must print exactly `11, 35, 133`. Note `133 = 2^7 + 5 = 2^3 + 5^3` is a genuine `A = 3` solution of the *integer* equation; it is even/even and composite — a useful reminder that primality, through the `A < X/√6` bound, is doing real work in that branch.
    
    ## 5. Where this leaves the proof
    
    The program makes the statement "no solution with `A > 1` below 256 digits" a certified computation, and the cascade shows where the structural arguments in your notes stop being sufficient: every surviving pair is ultimately killed by the window (N2) or the exact test (N9), i.e. by *size*, never by a congruence alone. That is the honest shape of the remaining gap. Two comments for the proof itself:
    
    1. The equation in the even/odd case is `q^{n1}(q^{Δn} − 1) = 2^{m2}(2^{Δm} − 1)`, a four-term `S`-unit equation in the primes `{2, q}`. Equations of exactly this form, `a^x − a^z = b^y − b^w`, have been treated with linear forms in logarithms; I recall a theorem of M. Bennett (*On some exponential equations of S. S. Pillai*, Canad. J. Math. 53, 2001) bounding the number of solutions for fixed bases, with the pairs `(2,3)` and `(2,5)` among the listed exceptions — consistent with the `11, 35, 133` above — but please check the exact statement; I am citing from memory. Baker-type bounds give an effective `Δm` ceiling for each `q`, and (N2) gives `q < 2^{Δm/3}`, so a finite computation of the kind above could in principle close the problem.
    
    2. Elementary leverage you have not yet used: `2^k + ε` (the cofactor coprime to `q^{n1}`) divides `A`, so `ord_{2^k+ε}(q) | Δn < 2k/log₂q`. A prime `q < 2^{2k/3}` having multiplicative order `< 2k` modulo a number of size `2^k` is the real obstruction; (N7) is its shadow on the small prime factors. A proof would have to turn that into a contradiction without knowing the factorisation of `2^k + ε` — which is exactly the stretch §6.7 (`r ≥ 5`) and this program leave open.

    # Covering sets — what was actually built (ground truth from artifacts)
    
    This reconciles a conflation I made. There were **two different experiments** with two
    different parameter regimes and two different results. I merged them and mis-reported.

    number is *not* re-confirmed this session, it is marked.
    
    ## Verified dataset facts (exact, read from `pk0.i64` / `kpos.i64` this session)
    
    - Test set: **100,000,000 primes** (the first 100M; largest is p_max = 2,038,074,659).
      **17,020,122** are k=0, **82,979,878** are k>0.
    - k=0 positions x = p − 2ᵐ: **508,730,655** with m ≥ 0 (2ᵐ < p — the instruction's rule),
      or **491,710,533** with m ≥ 1 (what the experiments used). ~29–30 per prime.

    ## The metric mismatch (the thing that actually matters)
    
    `instruction.md` scores **per-prime full coverage**: a prime counts only when *every*
    position x = p − 2ᵐ is covered. Targets: ≥ 99.99% of k=0, < 0.1% of k>0.

      (61, 71, 83, 109, 127, 173, …). A handful of small moduli can't reach them. Covering
      them all is exactly what forces the modulus set out to every prime ≤ √p_max — i.e. the
      certificate.
    
    So as `instruction.md` is currently written (per-prime, 99.99% / 0.1%), only **Covering B**
    qualifies. A 30–35 congruence covering does not meet those targets; it's a different
    (position-coverage) task.

    2026-03-18  Local-Global Periodicity: q-chains and fixed-modulus obstructions

    1. BIPARTITE (n, m) ADJACENCY FOR q=3
    
       The q=3 chain has 21 distinct n-values and 33 distinct m-values forming
       a bipartite graph.  All nodes belong to a single connected component --
       there are no isolated clusters.  This means every solution is reachable
       from every other by alternating n-steps and m-steps through shared edges.
    
       Degree distributions: n-degrees (number of m-values per n) vary from ~3
       to ~15.  m-degrees (number of n-values per m) vary from ~2 to ~12.
       Higher-degree nodes tend to have smaller m or n values, reflecting the
       higher prime density for smaller values of 2^m + 3^n.
    
    2. M-PAIR ARITHMETIC PROGRESSIONS
    
       Among (m1, m2) pairs that share n-values:
       - d=3 gives the longest AP: m = 1, 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22 (length 8).
       - d=12 APs (e.g., m = 4, 16, 28 sharing n = {1, 4, 12}) have the highest
         density of shared n-values per pair.
       - Other frequent deltas: d=1, d=2, d=6.
    
    3. OBSTRUCTION CROSS-LINES
    
       When 2^m + 3^n is composite (a "gap" in the q=3 chain), the composite
       value's smallest prime factor follows rigid patterns:
    
       - q'=5 causes 31.7% of gaps, with n-hits distributed by n mod 4
         (period = ord_5(3) = 4).
       - q'=7 causes 16.8% of gaps, with period-6 structure
         (period = ord_7(3) = 6).
       - q'=13: the m-values hit are spaced by d=12 = ord_13(2).
    
    4. CONNECTION TO fixed_mod.py: LOCAL OBSTRUCTIONS EXPLAIN GAP PERIODICITY
    
       The d=12 AP pattern in m-pair sharing and the d=12 spacing in q'=13
       obstructions are the SAME PHENOMENON.  The multiplicative order ord_{q'}(2)
       governs the periodicity of 2^m mod q', which determines when two m-values
       produce the same residue class and thus share the same local solvability.
    
       More precisely: for each small prime ell (not 2, not q), the values
       2^m + q^n mod ell depend only on (m mod ord_ell(2), n mod ord_ell(q)).
       This creates an obstruction grid of size ord_ell(2) x ord_ell(q).
       Cells where the sum is 0 mod ell are "killed" -- no prime > ell can
       arise from those (m, n) mod-classes.
    
       The gap periodicity seen in obstruction cross-lines is exactly this
       grid structure projected onto the m-axis (or n-axis).
    
    5. OPEN QUESTION: LOCAL-GLOBAL DISCREPANCY
    
       The sieve density -- the product of (1 - killed/total) across small
       primes ell -- predicts the fraction of (m, n) pairs surviving all local
       obstructions.  The empirical density is the fraction that actually yield
       primes.
    
       If empirical/sieve converges to a stable ratio as ell_max grows, the
       gaps are "explained" by local conditions (up to PNT scaling).  If there
       is a systematic discrepancy or the ratio oscillates, that signals global
       structure not captured by any finite set of moduli.

    2026-03-30  Covering-system characterization of obstructed primes
    -----------------------------------------------------------------
    
    Key insight: the obstruction mechanism is a covering system in the sense
    of Erdős.  For p = 2^m + q^n, if p is obstructed (k=0), then for every
    m in [1, floor(log2(p))], the remainder r = p - 2^m has at least two
    distinct prime factors (it's never a prime power).
    
    The propagation rule is:
      If q | p - 2^k  and  q | 2^m - 2^k,  then  q | p - 2^m.
    
    Since 2^m - 2^k = 2^k(2^{m-k} - 1), the odd part is always a Mersenne
    number M_d = 2^d - 1 where d = m - k.  Prime q divides M_d iff
    ord(2, q) | d.  So if q | p - 2^k, then q also divides p - 2^{k+j·ord(2,q)}
    for all j -- an arithmetic progression of "poisoned" m-values.
    
    An obstructed prime is one where these progressions COVER all valid m:
    
      [1, floor(log2(p))] ⊆ ⋃_i { k_i + j · ord(2, q_i) : j ≥ 0 }
    
    where each q_i | p - 2^{k_i}.
    
    EMPIRICAL RESULTS (499 obstructed primes, p up to ~30K):
      - 499/499 (100%) fully explained by covering systems of small primes
      - Covering set size distribution: mode = 5, range = [3, 8]
      - The backbone {3, 5, 7} with orders {2, 4, 3} appears in nearly all covers:
          q=3: 100%, q=5: 84%, q=7: 65%
      - LCM(2, 3, 4) = 12, so the backbone repeats with period 12
      - For small primes, {3, 5, 7} + a few helpers (11, 13, 17, ...) suffice
      - Residue classes mod 105 = 3·5·7 determine which backbone classes apply
    
    STRUCTURAL IMPLICATIONS:
      1. The "dual" of the q_k recurrence chains: those describe which q^n
         appear as solutions; covering systems describe why NO q^n can appear.
      2. The obstruction rate (~17.3%) should be computable as: the density
         of primes p such that the covering conditions are satisfiable,
         i.e., p mod q ≡ 2^{k_i} mod q for enough (q_i, k_i) pairs.
      3. Scalability: as p grows, max_m ~ log2(p), and the covering only
         needs log2(p) positions covered.  Since ord(2,3) = 2 already covers
         half, this grows very slowly in the number of primes needed.
    
    CONNECTION TO PRIOR WORK:
      - The d=12 periodicity noted 2026-03-18 (ord_13(2) = 12 in q'=13
        gap structure) is a special case of this covering mechanism.
      - Fixed-mod analysis (multiplicative orders governing gap periodicity)
        was seeing the same phenomenon from the solution side.

    2026-03-30  Subgroup exclusion proof for 22 unconditional obstruction classes
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    THEOREM PROVED(?): For the 22 residue classes r mod 255255 where the covering
    system {3,5,7,11,13,17} fully covers Z/12Z, every prime p ≡ r (mod 255255)
    is obstructed (k = 0).  This was verified computationally by a finite check
    (no heuristics, no sampling — purely algebraic).
    
    THE PROOF HAS THREE LEMMAS:
    
    Lemma 1 (Multi-coverage): At positions m mod 12 covered by ≥2 covering primes,
      p - 2^m has ≥2 distinct prime factors, so it's not a prime power.  Trivial.
    
    Lemma 2 (Covering completeness): For each of the 22 classes, the covering
      system covers all of Z/12Z.  The 8 multi-coverage positions are handled by
      Lemma 1.  The remaining 4 single-coverage positions (per class) are all
      covered by q=3 alone (q=11 positions are always multi-covered).
    
    Lemma 3 (Subgroup exclusion): At each single-coverage position m ≡ pos (mod 12)
      with covering prime q=3, for EVERY m in this congruence class, there exists
      a blocking prime ℓ such that:
        (p - 2^m) mod ℓ  ∉  ⟨3⟩ ⊂ (Z/ℓZ)*
      Since 3^n mod ℓ ∈ ⟨3⟩ for all n, p - 2^m ≠ 3^n.
    
    MECHANISM: 3 is not a primitive root mod certain primes, so ⟨3⟩ is a proper
    subgroup of (Z/ℓZ)*.  The forced residue (p - 2^m) mod ℓ, determined by the
    congruence class r mod 255255, falls outside this subgroup — a contradiction
    if we assume p - 2^m = 3^n.
    
    BLOCKING PRIMES NEEDED: {13, 37, 41, 61, 67, 73, 181, 193}
      - ℓ=13 handles most cases: ord(3,13) = 3, index 4 (excludes 75% of residues)
      - ℓ=41: ord(3,41) = 8, index 5 (excludes 80%)
      - ℓ=61: ord(3,61) = 10, index 6 (excludes 83%)
      - ℓ=73: ord(3,73) = 12, index 6 (excludes 83%)
      - ℓ=193: ord(3,193) = 16, index 12 (excludes 92%)
      - Maximum blocking prime: 193
    
    HARDEST CASE: Class (1,3,2,7,5,15) at m≡2 (mod 12) required 4 blocking
    primes {193, 181, 67, 41} with a combined period of 1320 to close.
    Most positions are blocked by ℓ=13 alone (period 1 — all m blocked at once).
    
    STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION: The single-coverage prime is ALWAYS q=3 (never q=11).
    All q=11 positions have at least one other covering prime (multi-covered).
    This means the proof reduces entirely to showing 3^n can't match at 4
    positions per class, using the subgroup structure of ⟨3⟩ in (Z/ℓZ)*.
    
    VERIFICATION STATISTICS:
      22 classes × 4 single positions = 88 position-class pairs
      68/88 blocked by ℓ=13 alone (period 1)
      20/88 need additional primes (periods up to 1320)
      Total finite checks: bounded, all pass

          prime-power-density weight 1/ln(q^n) gives a principled, non-uniform
          per-position hit probability (replacing the uniform 1.88/m). Directly
          checkable against the stored (q, n).

    ## 2. The chain of necessary conditions (synthesis)
    
    All of these are proved in your notes; I list them in the order a decision procedure should apply them, with the sections they come from, and I note two places where they sharpen each other.

    **(N1) Size.** `Δn ≥ 3`, hence `q³ ≤ q^Δn < 2^Δm`, hence `Δm ≥ 6` (§9.3, §9.4). `m2 = v2(q−1) ≤ k` (E3). `q^n1` divides exactly one of `2^k ∓ 1`, so `q^n1 ≤ 2^k+1` and `A ≥ 2^k−1` (§5.6).

This subsumes (N5) (`ℓ ∤ 2^Δm−1` is the case RHS `< 0`).
    
    **(N7) Odd-order closure.** For every prime `ℓ | 2^Δm−1`, `ℓ ≠ q`: `ord_ℓ(q)` is odd and `ord_ℓ(q) | Δn`; more precisely `ord_{ℓ^e}(q) | Δn` for `ℓ^e ∥ 2^Δm−1` (§5.4, §10.2). Equivalently `ord_A(q) | Δn`. (N3) is the instance `ℓ = 3`.

    * (N0)–(N8) are all functions of `(q, Δm)` plus, for the last ones, a short list of admissible `Δn` (odd multiples of `lcm(L, ∏ ℓ^{t_ℓ})` inside the window of (N2)). None of them needs the cofactor `A` built, and none needs `2^Δm−1` factored — only its *known* small prime factors, which we get for free (below).

    ## 3. The decision procedure
    
    Fix `M = ⌊256·log₂10⌋ = 850` (so `m1 ≤ M`) and a threshold `Q` (default `2^32`).
    
    **Stage S (`q ≤ Q`).** Every solution with `q ≤ Q` has `ord_q(2) | Δm ≤ M−1`. So scan all primes `q ≤ Q`, compute `ord_q(2)` (factor `q−1` with `n_factor`), keep those with order `≤ M−1`. This list is simultaneously (a) the complete candidate list for Stage S and (b) the complete list of primes `ℓ ≤ Q` dividing any `2^Δm−1`, i.e. the "known prime support" needed for (N7). For each candidate `q` and each even `Δm` in `ord_q(2)·ℤ` with `m2+Δm ≤ M`, run the cascade (N1)→(N9) and record the first condition that fails. This is §5.3 + §8 + §9 + §10 run to `Δm = 849`, with no factoring.
    
    **Stage L (`q > Q`).** Here `n2 = n1 + Δn` is tiny: `Q^n2 < q^n2 ≤ 1.5·(2^m1 − 2^m2)` gives `n2 ≤ (m1+0.585)/log₂Q ≤ 26`, while (N1) gives `n2 ≥ 4` and `n2 > 3(m1−1)/Δm`. For fixed `(Δm, m2, n2)` the base is forced: `N < q^n2 ≤ 1.5N` has the unique integer solution `q = ⌈N^{1/n2}⌉`, so one `fmpz_root` per triple decides it (`q^n2 − N` must be a pure power `q^n1`). Roughly `2·10^6` roots for `M = 850`.
    
    Together the two stages exhaust all `p < 10^256` in the even/odd case, and Stage S additionally tells you *why* each `(q, Δm)` dies. The program also runs the raw §5.3 one-shot test ("oracle") on every Stage-S pair independently of the filters and aborts loudly if a filter ever contradicts it, so a mistake in any filter cannot silently lose a solution.

    Everything in the notes collapses, once it is put in order, into **one statement about two integers**. That is what the program below implements; no other search space is needed.
    
    ## 0. Reduction to the even/odd case (closing the A = 1 hole)
    
    Let `p > 3` be prime with `p = 2^m1 + q^n1 = 2^m2 + q^n2`, `m1 > m2 ≥ 1`, `n2 > n1 ≥ 1`, `q` an odd prime, `Δm = m1−m2`, `Δn = n2−n1`,
    
    ```
    A q^n1 = 2^Δm − 1,   A 2^m2 = q^Δn − 1,   Ap = 2^Δm q^Δn − 1.
    ```
    
    * **R1 (Δm even).** mod‑3 parity funnel: `3 | p − 2^m` for exactly one parity class of `m`; two representations with the *same* `q` must sit on the same side, so `m1 ≡ m2 (mod 2)`.
    * **R2 (A = 1 ⇒ p = 11, with a complete proof).** `A = 1` means `q^{n1} = 2^Δm − 1` and `q^{Δn} = 2^{m2} + 1`.
     – If `Δn ≥ 2`, Mihăilescu forces `q^{Δn} = 9, 2^{m2} = 8`, i.e. `q = 3, Δn = 2, m2 = 3`; then `3^{n1} = 2^Δm − 1` forces `n1 = 1, Δm = 2` (Mihăilescu again), giving `p = 2^5 + 3 = 35`, not prime.
     – So `Δn = 1` and `q = 2^{m2} + 1`. Likewise `q^{n1} = 2^Δm − 1` with `n1 ≥ 2` is impossible (Mihăilescu), so `n1 = 1` and `q = 2^Δm − 1`. Then `2^Δm − 2^{m2} = 2`, i.e. `m2 = 1, Δm = 2, q = 3`, and `p = 2^3 + 3 = 2 + 3^2 = 11`.
     **So `p = 11` is the complete `A = 1` answer; from here on `A > 1`.**
    * **R3 (Δn odd).** With `Δm` even, `Δn` even would give `d = gcd(Δm,Δn)` even, and §6.4 (`Φ_d(Y) | Y^{d/2}+1`, hence `A ≥ Y^{d/2} − 1`, against `A < Y^{d/2}/√6`) closes it — the `d = 2` instance is the difference‑of‑squares obstruction.
    
    So the **only open configuration is exactly the one in the notes**: `A > 1`, `Δm = 2k` even, `Δn` odd. Everything below assumes it. (Note the search never assumes `gcd(Δm,Δn)=1`, so the open branch §6.7 costs us nothing computationally.)
    
    ## 1. The pair `(q, Δm)` determines the whole configuration
    
    From §5.1, §5.2, §5.6:
    
    ```
    q is a prime factor of 2^Δm − 1,        n1 = v_q(2^Δm − 1),   A = (2^Δm − 1)/q^{n1},
    m2 = v2(q − 1),                          m1 = m2 + Δm,
    q^{n1} | (2^k − 1)(2^k + 1) with q^{n1} inside exactly one factor ⇒ q^{n1} ≤ 2^k + 1, A ≥ 2^k − 1, m2 ≤ k.
    ```
    
    Hence **a configuration exists for `(q,Δm)` iff the single number**
    
    ```
    T(q,Δm) := A·2^{m2} + 1       is an odd power of q,  T = q^{Δn}, Δn ≥ 3,
    ```
    
    and then `n2 = n1 + Δn`, `p = 2^{m2} + q^{n2}`, `m1 = ⌊log2 p⌋`, `n2 = ⌊log_q p⌋` (§9.1). The four‑parameter search `(m1,m2,n1,n2)` is gone: **two integers, one test.**

    | S7 | parity of `n1 = v_q(2^Δm−1)`: `q≡3 (8) ⇒ n1` odd, `q≡7 (8) ⇒ n1` even | §7.1, §7.2 |

    | S11 | exact: `T = A·2^{m2}+1 = q^{Δn}` | §5.3 |

    * **Window width.** `q^{Δn} = A2^{m2}+1 ≥ (2^k−1)2^{m2}+1` and `q^{Δn} < 2^{2k}` give

Since `q^{n1} ≤ 2^k+1`, "`q` large" and "`n1` large" are the same thing; the window is empty precisely in the regime where `q^{n1}` fills up `2^k±1`.
    * **The Mersenne corner is the only escape.** S8 is a closure condition *internal to `2^Δm−1`*; it fails as soon as `2^Δm−1` is prime‑rich.
